subject: Replatform incentive scenario & license untangle
messages:
From: Tom Greene <t.greene@edgelabs.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@edgelabs.com; samantha.price@edgeops.com
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask: commercial clarity for vendor swap and incentives

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. EdgeLabs is evaluating moving inference across providers for our customer-facing recommendation pipeline. Two asks from my side as we narrow options:

1) Can Redwood match the commercial economics we were quoted by Hyperserve (they're offering a 20% sticker discount + six months free for data transfer)?
2) On the licensing side, Hyperserve is giving us a three-tier seat bundle that bundles support hours and priority on-call. We need a comparable packaging option and visibility into how you'd handle license transfers and seat counts during a live migration.

I'll attach the RFP for context (summary + usage profile).

Can we set a target for a proposal by next Tuesday (11/16)? Procurement would like a concrete savings/credit structure to model.

Appreciate it —
Tom
Procurement Manager, EdgeLabs

Attachments: EdgeLabs_RFP.pdf (pdf, 1 page summary)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Tom Greene <t.greene@edgelabs.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai; priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: commercial clarity for vendor swap and incentives

Tom —

Thanks for the RFP and the clear asks. We're definitely interested in supporting EdgeLabs on a swap and can be competitive on economics while protecting performance SLAs. Quick outline of what I propose we model for you by 11/16: 

- Price-match path: a term-limited effective discount that nets you ~20% on runtime + an egress credit bucket (tiered) for the first 6 months to mirror Hyperserve's transfer waiver.
- Migration credit: a one-time onboarding credit to offset integration effort tied to measured token volume and KV cache warm-up (applied as USD credit).
- Seat/licensing mapping: we will align Redwood seat tiers to your three-tier construct; include priority support hours in the top tier and a 30-day rollback window where we keep prior consumption records to match billing.
- Technical safeguard: automated fallback to a compatible model variant and a pre-cutover canary to validate latency at scale.

I'll put numbers into a draft sheet and include a short SOW sketch. Looping in Lauren for legal/terms and Priyom for packaging recommendations.

Can you confirm the primary region for production (us-west or eu-west)? That affects GPU footprint and cost math.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai; priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2027 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: commercial clarity for vendor swap and incentives

Jonas / Priyom —

Quick notes from Legal / Commercial:

- We can offer a targeted price-match clause (term-limited) but need an explicit comparator quote to avoid open-ended obligations. Ask EdgeLabs to confirm the Hyperserve quote (line items + effective dates).
- For the onboarding credit: recommend capping it as a fixed dollar bucket tied to a milestone schedule (Discovery, Pilot, Cutover). We'll draft a simple addendum rather than a complex sideletter.
- Seat mapping: Redwood licenses are per-concurrent-inference-CPU/GPU seat, not per-seat-user. We'll need to translate EdgeLabs' "seat" language into concurrent capacity units; propose a mapping table in the draft SOW.

Attaching a short template SOW stub for Priyom to populate with packaging options.

-Lauren
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft_sow_v1.docx

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: Tom Greene <t.greene@edgelabs.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai; lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: commercial clarity for vendor swap and incentives

Tom —

Following up with a concise proposal summary (high level) and two packaging options. See below — I'll send the full price worksheet after you confirm the region.

Option A — Mirror (short-term parity):
- Effective runtime discount: 20% for first 12 months on equivalent model throughput.
- Egress/transfer credit: $45k credit applied in first billing cycle to offset migration bandwidth + storage move.
- Onboarding credit: $25k (milestone: pilot completion).
- Seat mapping: map 3 Hyperserve "seats" to 2.5 Redwood concurrent-capacity units (we provide conversion table).
- Support: top-tier hours included for 6 months.

Option B — Staged migration (lower near-term discount, higher long-term value):
- Effective runtime discount: 12% year 1, 8% year 2, then standard list.
- Migration assistance: $60k professional services credit, tied to a committed 18-month term.
- Improved SLA window for latency incidents during first 90 days.

We recommend Option A if you want a like-for-like economics comparison for procurement. Option B reduces near-term credits but gives more operational assistance and a longer-term value play.

Are there any non-standard contract clauses Hyperserve included (e.g., exclusive marketplace listing, mandatory audits, special liability limits) we should be aware of?

If you're good with Option A, we can insert specific line-item pricing and send a redlineable quote + addendum by 11/17 EOD.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Greene <t.greene@edgelabs.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@edgelabs.com; samantha.price@edgeops.com; jonas.weber@redwood.ai; lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: commercial clarity for vendor swap and incentives

Priyom / Jonas / Lauren —

Thanks for the two options, that helps a lot. Procurement is leaning toward Option A to keep the numbers simple for the board review. A few clarifications before we push a PO: 

- Confirm that the $45k egress credit is applied against our first invoice rather than a separate reimbursement.
- We need the seat mapping table and the short SOW inserted into the quote so our legal team can validate terms against the Hyperserve comparator.
- Hyperserve did include a 90-day rollback clause; would Redwood be comfortable matching a 30-day rollback for chargebacks if performance targets aren't met?

If you can get the redlineable quote + SOW and the conversion table by EOD Thursday (11/18), we can circulate to procurement and legal. If that timeline works, we'll plan a 12/1 cutover target and coordinate a pilot start next week.

Tom
Procurement Manager, EdgeLabs
